questions.question_text:
A backyard is a rectangle with dimensions $14.5\text{ m}$ by $8\text{ m}$. It contains a triangular pool with base $5\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $3\text{ m}$, and a square patio with side length $2.5\text{ m}$. The pool and patio do not overlap.
What is the remaining area of the yard to the nearest whole square metre?

options.why: Found only the whole yard area, $14.5\times8=116$, without subtracting the pool or patio.
Forgot to halve the pool's base times height, giving $116-15-6.25=94.75$, which rounds to $95$.
Subtracted the pool area but left out the patio, giving $116-7.5=108.5$, which rounds to $109$.

questions.solution_text:
Yard area: $14.5\times8=116\text{ m}^2$.
Pool area: $5\times3\div2=7.5\text{ m}^2$.
Patio area: $2.5\times2.5=6.25\text{ m}^2$.
$A=116-7.5-6.25$
$=102.25\text{ m}^2$
To the nearest whole square metre, the remaining area is $102\text{ m}^2$.

questions.question_text:
An L-shaped room has all right angles. Its total height is $6\text{ m}$ and its upper section is $2\text{ m}$ wide. The lower section extends $3\text{ m}$ beyond the upper section and is $2\text{ m}$ high.
What is the floor area in $\text{m}^2$?

options.why: Used the whole surrounding rectangle, $(2+3)\times6=30$, without removing the missing corner.
Added the full-height rectangle and the full lower rectangle, $2\times6+5\times2=22$, counting their shared $2\text{ m}$ by $2\text{ m}$ area twice.
Found only the lower rectangle, $(2+3)\times2=10$, and left out the upper part.

questions.solution_text:
Split the room into the full-height rectangle and the lower extension.
$A=A_1+A_2$
$=2\times6+3\times2$
$=12+6$
$=18\text{ m}^2$
